input.rationale: Both open questions are settled (commit eligibility refuted the non-voter suspicion with a retained witness; the AddVoter configuration lag was explained as a bounded transient). I reselected along the same axes onto the history/persistence mechanism that the earlier work leaned on but never examined directly: whether a restarted node reuses its durable last-vote (term plus candidate) so that a single node cannot cast two different votes in one term. Reading the restart path and the vote handler gives a concrete, cheaply testable account, and the registered discriminator uses only real producers (a real RequestVote RPC through the node's transport consumer and a real restart over the same stores). This turn is source-only; no measured interpretation is claimed without the receipt.

investigations.question: After a restart, does a node reuse its durable last-vote (term and candidate) so that it cannot grant a second, different vote in the same term, and does its restored currentTerm still deny votes from older terms?
investigations.hypothesis: The vote is recorded in StableStore before the response is granted, and restart restores only currentTerm and the last log entry, not any in-memory vote state; therefore the same-term duplicate decision is made from the durable last-vote keys and survives a restart, while the restored currentTerm denies older-term requests.
investigations.discriminator: In one process, with a real InmemStore-backed node, send a RequestVote for candidate A in term T through the node's transport consumer and confirm it is granted (the node persists LastVoteTerm=T/LastVoteCand=A); restart the node over the same stores; then require that a RequestVote for a different candidate B in the same term T is denied, that a repeat request for A in term T is still granted, and that any candidate in a term below T is denied. The predicate is the granted flag plus the term actually reached, not the response text.

knowledge.statement: The same-term duplicate-vote decision is read from durable storage on every RequestVote: the handler loads LastVoteTerm and LastVoteCand from StableStore, grants only when the stored candidate bytes equal the requesting candidate, and otherwise returns without granting. persistVote writes the term key before the candidate key and is called before Granted is set, so no acknowledged vote depends on in-memory state and a restart does not reset the last vote.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3 node receiving a RequestVote RPC whose term is not older than the node's currentTerm and whose candidate is a Voter in the node's latest configuration.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only account of the restart/vote relationship. On startup the node restores currentTerm from the CurrentTerm stable key and the last log entry through setCurrentTerm/setLastLog, and nothing else vote-related is restored, so any same-term duplicate decision must come from the durable keys. In the vote handler the duplicate check reads LastVoteTerm and LastVoteCand from StableStore, returns granted only when the stored candidate bytes equal the requesting candidate, and otherwise returns without setting Granted, so a second different candidate in the same term is denied regardless of restart. persistVote writes the term first and then the candidate before the handler sets Granted, so an acknowledged vote is durable before the response. The older-term rejection is the earlier term comparison, and the restored currentTerm is what makes it effective after a restart. This is a source-explained negative - a protection that defeats an obvious candidate defect - so no defect is asserted and the discriminator is left for execution rather than inferred from reading.
limitations: Source-only: the restart behaviour is read from the constructors and handlers, not yet observed; in particular the claim that a new Raft instance does not consult any other persisted vote artefact rests on reading NewRaft and restoreSnapshot.
The account covers the vote path only; it does not evaluate whether a restart can otherwise reuse stale term or log state in a way that breaks safety (for example a truncated log tail).

knowledge.statement: On the leader, appendConfigurationEntry stores the new configuration log entry via dispatchLogs, then sets r.configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls commitment.setConfiguration(new), which rebuilds the commit voter set and recalculates the commit index. Commit of later entries is therefore evaluated over the new configuration's voters, and the leader's own latest configuration is updated at append time rather than at commit time.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in Leader state; configurationChangeChIfStable gated (latestIndex == committedIndex and a commit of the current term already observed); protocolVersion 3 so the entry is a LogConfiguration; prevIndex match in nextConfiguration.

knowledge.statement: nextConfiguration's AddNonvoter case does not demote an existing member: if the server ID already exists with Suffrage other than Nonvoter, only its Address is updated and its Voter/Staging suffrage is retained; a new server is appended as Nonvoter. Demotion of an existing voter is only reachable through DemoteVoter.
knowledge.conditions: protocol-version-3 ID-based configuration change request with a client-supplied server ID that already exists in the current configuration.

knowledge.statement: On a follower, appendEntries stores accepted new entries and then calls processConfigurationLogEntry for each stored configuration entry, which sets configurations.latest/latestIndex to the newly decoded configuration at store time, before the entry's commit index is known. configurations.latest is therefore the locally stored (possibly uncommitted) configuration, and GetConfiguration on any node reports it without consulting the main thread.
knowledge.conditions: Follower receiving AppendEntries whose entries are new or whose conflicting suffix was deleted; protocol 3 LogConfiguration entries (or deprecated peer entries); configurations.latest is updated from the follower's own log store, independent of LeaderCommitIndex.

knowledge.statement: On the leader, the commit set is built exclusively from servers whose Suffrage is Voter: newCommitment and commitment.setConfiguration insert a matchIndexes entry only for Voter servers, commitment.match updates an index only if the reporting server is already a key in matchIndexes, and recalculate takes the majority-order element of those values. Replication goroutines, by contrast, are started for every server in configurations.latest regardless of suffrage, and quorumSize and checkLeaderLease also count only Voters. Consequently an acknowledgement from a Nonvoter/Staging server cannot advance commitIndex, and processLogs applies to the FSM only entries up to the leader's commitIndex.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; protocol version 3 configuration with mixed suffrage; the leader's commitment was built from configurations.latest at leader setup and rebuilt on each committed/appended configuration change.

result.summary: Kept this cycle source-only (the restart/durable-vote experiment needs a custom restart-over-existing-stores harness and no Restart helper exists in the snapshot's test scaffolding, so I did not submit an unverified harness). Added the durable Behavior @k_durable_last_vote: the same-term duplicate-vote decision is read from StableStore on every RequestVote (LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand), granting only for the identical stored candidate, with persistVote writing term then candidate before the grant is set, and restart restoring only currentTerm and the last log entry, so the last vote survives a restart. The registered investigation @q_restart_vote and its source-only interpretation (explained, no defect asserted) remain unchanged, with the discriminator ready for execution next cycle.
